Easy Fix - Before replacing turn off your gas line and unplug your oven.

Oven had stopped working with the baking option. This part fixed the problem quickly. I would advise to remove the oven door do make it easier to work on, do this by opening the door to the first notch and pull up. If your oven is not turning on when selecting the baking option you will want to replace the igniter on the bottom, it will probably be under a panel. My oven had two screws inside at the back that needed to be removed to remove the panel. Once the panel was removed it was in plain sight. I would suggest removing the screw on the gas tube so it is easier to reach the screws that hold the igniter in place. You will need to use a wire cutter made to remove the outside shell of the wire to splice the old and new wire together. I only had to splice one of the wires, the other fit perfectly like it was.

All I needed to for the job was a wire cutter, 1/4" socket and a flashlight.

Worked well with additional repair steps - Used this to mend our washing machine. The drive splines on the metal shaft rusted a lot and consequently tore up this piece. That metal assembly is no longer available (machine is only 4 years old). I cleaned the shaft after disassembly with a wire wheel. I then coated the inside of this plastic gear with candle wax. After assembling the machine to the point of needing this gear I mixed up JB Weld fast set and spread it onto the metal shaft thoroughly pressing it into the pores. Then I slid this gear onto the shaft. The wax concept is to prevent the epoxy from binding to the gear should I need to make a future repair. Otherwise good luck getting it apart. Washing machines are too expensive to replace. You're paying a lot for old tech. The machines just look fancier and have more computer controls.. controls that rely on more sensors... sensors that essentially still rely on the same basic drive motor and gear assembly.

Easy to install - If the start switch on your compactor is broken, and this is the correct part for your model, go for it. Very easy install on my Whirlpool GX900QPLB0

1. Unplug compactor, or turn off at breaker but make sure power is OFF
2. Open compactor drawer
3. Remove 2 screws under the control panel
4. Lift control panel up slightly, then off
5. Mark the cables so you know where they reattach on new switch, or do what I did and take a pic with your phone
6. Remove the cables from old switch
7. Attach to new switch
8. Slide control panel back into place
9. Replace two screws under control panel
10.Plug compactor in, or turn on breaker

That's it!
